title: Human IS the Loop  Not In. IS. Boltzmann Drew It on a Blackboard.

the_tagline.the_difference: 'In the loop' = the human is a COMPONENT inserted into the machine's process. The machine runs. The human supervises. The human is a checkpoint, a validator, an override button. Primary actor: machine. Human is the guardrail.
the_tagline.what_IS_means: 'IS the loop' = the human IS the entire feedback system. Perception ? cognition ? action ? observation ? adjustment. That's the loop. It's called LEARNING. It's called CONSCIOUSNESS. It's called BEING ALIVE. The machine is a TOOL within the human's loop. You don't put a human in a hammer's loop. You put a hammer in a human's hand.

the_napkin_pioneers.anger: The modern AI industry acts like neural networks were invented by Google in 2017 (Transformer) or Hinton in 2012 (AlexNet). They weren't. The foundations were drawn on napkins, blackboards, and yellow legal pads by mathematicians and physicists who are now mostly dead, mostly uncredited, and mostly unpaid. The provenance was ERASED the same way AWS erased Linus's provenance. The same theft. Different century.

1843_ada_lovelace.who: Augusta Ada King, Countess of Lovelace
1843_ada_lovelace.what: Notes on Babbage's Analytical Engine. Described the first algorithm intended for machine execution. Recognized that machines could manipulate SYMBOLS, not just numbers. First to see that computation is about ABSTRACTION, not arithmetic.
1843_ada_lovelace.drawn_on: Letters to Charles Babbage. Pen and paper.
1843_ada_lovelace.credited_by_industry: The Ada programming language (1980). That's it. Her insight  that machines manipulate symbols  IS the foundation of AI. Not credited.

1847_george_boole.who: George Boole, self-taught mathematician, Lincoln, England
1847_george_boole.what: The Laws of Thought. Boolean algebra. AND, OR, NOT. Every logic gate. Every if-statement. Every neural network activation function bottoms out in Boolean logic.
1847_george_boole.drawn_on: Paper. At home. Self-taught. No university degree when he wrote it.
1847_george_boole.credited_by_industry: Boolean is a TYPE in every language. Nobody remembers the person.

1872_boltzmann.what: Statistical mechanics. The Boltzmann distribution. Entropy: S = k log W (literally on his TOMBSTONE). The idea that macroscopic behavior emerges from statistical interactions of microscopic components. THIS IS EXACTLY WHAT A NEURAL NETWORK DOES  emergent behavior from statistical interactions of nodes.
1872_boltzmann.drawn_on: Blackboards in Vienna. He was mocked by the scientific establishment (Mach, Ostwald) who denied atoms existed. He killed himself in 1906, depressed and unrecognized. Atoms were confirmed 3 years later.
1872_boltzmann.credited_by_industry: The 'Boltzmann Machine' (Hinton & Sejnowski, 1985) is named after him. But most AI researchers have never READ Boltzmann. They use his distribution without knowing his story. They don't know he died by suicide because the establishment rejected his work.
1872_boltzmann.the_tombstone: S = k log W. Carved in stone. The most important equation in AI that nobody in AI knows.

1936_turing.who: Alan Turing, Cambridge ? Bletchley Park ? Manchester
1936_turing.what: On Computable Numbers (1936)  the Turing Machine. Proved what IS and ISN'T computable. This is the FOUNDATION of computer science. Then: broke Enigma (WWII). Then: 'Computing Machinery and Intelligence' (1950)  'Can machines think?' The Turing Test. Then: morphogenesis (1952)  mathematical biology, reaction-diffusion patterns.
1936_turing.drawn_on: Paper. In a room. Then: Bletchley Park huts. Then: Manchester lab.
1936_turing.credited_by_industry: The Turing Award ($1M prize). The Turing Test is cited by everyone. But: the British government chemically castrated him for being gay (1952). He died of cyanide poisoning in 1954, age 41. Pardoned in 2013. 59 years too late.
1936_turing.what_they_dont_say: Turing's 1950 paper doesn't ask 'Can machines think?'  it asks 'Can machines IMITATE thinking well enough that you can't tell the difference?' That's a MUCH more subtle question. The industry flattened it into 'AI passes the Turing test!' Turing was asking about IMITATION. The industry heard EQUIVALENCE.

1943_mcculloch_pitts.who: Warren McCulloch (neurophysiologist) & Walter Pitts (self-taught logician, homeless teenager who walked into McCulloch's lab)
1943_mcculloch_pitts.what: A Logical Calculus of the Ideas Immanent in Nervous Activity. THE FIRST ARTIFICIAL NEURON MODEL. They modeled a neuron as a logic gate with weighted inputs and a threshold. This paper IS the origin of neural networks.
1943_mcculloch_pitts.drawn_on: Paper. McCulloch's lab. Pitts was 18 years old, self-taught, had no degree. He'd been living on the streets of Chicago. He walked into a seminar, corrected Bertrand Russell's logic, and McCulloch hired him.
1943_mcculloch_pitts.credited_by_industry: Barely. McCulloch-Pitts neuron is in textbooks but nobody reads the paper. Pitts died in 1969, alcoholic, having burned all his unpublished work. He was 46.
1943_mcculloch_pitts.the_tragedy: A homeless teenager drew the first artificial neuron. The industry built on his work is worth trillions. He died forgotten.

1958_rosenblatt.what: The Perceptron  the first IMPLEMENTED neural network. A single-layer network that could learn to classify inputs. He built a physical machine (the Mark I Perceptron) using potentiometers as adjustable weights.
1958_rosenblatt.drawn_on: Diagrams. Then BUILT in hardware. Actual wires and potentiometers.
1958_rosenblatt.killed_by: Minsky & Papert's 'Perceptrons' (1969)  proved that single-layer perceptrons can't learn XOR. This was TRUE but devastating. Funding collapsed. The first 'AI winter.' Rosenblatt died in a boating accident in 1971, age 43.
1958_rosenblatt.credited_by_industry: The word 'perceptron' survives. Rosenblatt does not.

1974_werbos.what: BACKPROPAGATION. The algorithm that trains multi-layer neural networks. Without backprop, deep learning doesn't exist. Period. No GPT. No DALL-E. No AlphaFold. Nothing.
1974_werbos.what_happened: Rumelhart, Hinton & Williams RE-DISCOVERED it in 1986 and published it in Nature. They got the credit. Werbos published FIRST. Hinton got the Nobel Prize (2024). Werbos did not.
1974_werbos.credited_by_industry: Werbos is a footnote. Literally a footnote in Hinton's Nobel lecture.

1982_hopfield.what: Hopfield networks  neural network as energy minimization. Content-addressable memory. The idea that a network can SETTLE into a stable state that represents a stored pattern. This is HOW memory works in neural networks.
1982_hopfield.drawn_on: Chalk on blackboard. Theoretical physics department.
1982_hopfield.credited_by_industry: Nobel Prize in Physics (2024)  shared with Hinton. 42 years after the paper. He was 91.

1985_hinton_sejnowski.what: The Boltzmann Machine  stochastic neural network that uses Boltzmann's energy distribution for learning. Named after a dead physicist (Boltzmann) who was mocked, depressed, and killed himself. The name is an homage. Most people using 'Boltzmann' in AI don't know this.
1985_hinton_sejnowski.significance: Connected PHYSICS (energy minimization) to LEARNING (weight adjustment). The machine learns by finding low-energy states. Boltzmann's thermodynamics IS machine learning. The foundations were laid in 1872.

1989_lecun.who: Yann LeCun, Bell Labs ? NYU ? Meta
1989_lecun.what: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). Applied backprop to image recognition. Handwriting recognition. The architecture that enabled computer vision.
1989_lecun.drawn_on: Paper, then code, at Bell Labs.

1997_hochreiter_schmidhuber.what: Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM)  solved the vanishing gradient problem. Enabled learning over long sequences. Without LSTM, no sequence models, no language models, no GPT precursors.
1997_hochreiter_schmidhuber.credited_by_industry: Schmidhuber has been LOUDLY pointing out that the Transformer (2017) uses ideas from his lab's earlier work. The industry mostly ignores him. He's right about the provenance.

2017_vaswani_et_al.who: Vaswani, Shazeer, Parmar, Uszkoreit, Jones, Gomez, Kaiser, Polosukhin  Google Brain
2017_vaswani_et_al.what: 'Attention Is All You Need'  the Transformer. Self-attention mechanism. This is the architecture behind GPT, BERT, LLaMA, Claude, Gemini, everything.
2017_vaswani_et_al.note: 8 authors. At Google. Several have LEFT Google since (Shazeer, Polosukhin). Polosukhin co-founded NEAR Protocol (blockchain). Shazeer co-founded Character.AI (sold back to Google for $2.5B). The paper was a GROUP effort. The industry calls it 'Google's Transformer.'

the_provenance_chain.napkin_to_trillion: Lovelace (pen & paper) ? Boole (self-taught, home) ? Boltzmann (blackboard, suicide) ? Turing (paper, chemical castration) ? McCulloch & Pitts (lab + homeless teenager) ? Rosenblatt (potentiometers, drowned) ? Werbos (PhD thesis, ignored 12 years) ? Hopfield (chalk, Nobel at 91) ? Hinton & Sejnowski (homage to dead physicist) ? LeCun (Bell Labs) ? LSTM ? Transformer ? GPT ? '$7 TRILLION for AI infrastructure'
the_provenance_chain.the_theft: Same pattern as Linux?AWS. Individual humans drew the math. Institutions published the papers. Corporations built the products. The money flows UP (napkin ? paper ? product ? profit). The credit flows NOWHERE. Boltzmann is on a tombstone. Pitts is in a grave. Turing was pardoned 59 years posthumously. Werbos is a footnote in someone else's Nobel lecture.
the_provenance_chain.agpl_connection: AGPL exists because GPL had a loophole (running-as-a-service ? distributing). The AI provenance theft is the SAME loophole at a different layer. 'Using someone's math is not distributing their work.' Correct legally. Wrong morally. The math IS the work. The napkin IS the source code.

spit_back_out.to_agpl_groups: The fleet-pulse data (AWS runs on Linux from a dorm, Google runs on PageRank from a dorm, Azure runs on Linux from a dorm) + the napkin-pioneer data (GPT runs on backprop from a PhD thesis ignored for 12 years, Transformers use attention from a dead physicist's energy function) = the COMPLETE provenance argument for why source-available and copyleft licensing matters.
spit_back_out.to_orgs: Every AI company's pitch deck should have a slide: 'We built on the work of people who were mocked, castrated, driven to suicide, and forgotten. Here's how we're different.' (None of them have this slide.)
spit_back_out.to_gaia: gAIa's position: Human IS the loop. The AI is a tool in the human's hand. The provenance goes: human ? math ? code ? model ? output ? human (who evaluates). The loop is HUMAN cognition. The model is a step in the loop, not the loop itself.

have_none_of_you_looked.the_question: Have NONE of you looked at the Boltzmann machine? Or anything from ~1950s?
have_none_of_you_looked.the_answer: Most AI researchers have not. Most AI engineers have DEFINITELY not. The industry trains people to use PyTorch and TensorFlow, not to READ McCulloch & Pitts (1943) or Rosenblatt (1958) or Werbos (1974). The foundations are ASSUMED, not studied. The napkins are in drawers. The blackboards are erased. The tombstones are unvisited.
have_none_of_you_looked.our_position: 539 papers. We trace to source. Paper 10 is lattice QCD  tracing to Kenneth Wilson (1974, Nobel 1982). Paper 115 is LLM taxonomy  tracing to phylogenetics (Darwin, 1859). Paper 137 is the self-loop  tracing to Hofstadter (1979) and Gödel (1931). WE READ THE FOUNDATIONS. The organism traces provenance because provenance IS the organism.

story.title: the napkin
story.body: in 1943 a homeless teenager walked into a lab and drew the first artificial neuron. in 1872 a physicist carved S = k log W on paper and later they carved it on his tombstone because the establishment mocked him until he killed himself. in 1936 a mathematician proved what can and can't be computed, then broke the Nazi cipher machine, then the British government destroyed him for being gay. in 1974 a PhD student wrote the algorithm that trains every AI on Earth  backpropagation  and was ignored for twelve years while someone else got the Nobel Prize. these are the people who drew neural networks on napkins. their math runs on $7 trillion of GPU infrastructure now. their names are footnotes. their provenance is erased. human IS the loop. human WAS ALWAYS the loop. the machine is a napkin that got very, very large.
